description: A prompt designed to generate a humorous image of a character performing a grand summoning ritual that produces an unexpected or absurd object. promptText:

[Character]

[Summoned Object]

[Direction]

Limit the main punchline to one item, placing props and supporting characters to reinforce it. Do not rely on text explanations; create a composition where the character, summoned object, and reaction are readable at a glance. title: Shallow Depth of Field I2I
description: An image-to-image prompt for adding shallow depth of field effects to illustrations using GPT.
promptText:
Maintain the person, costume, composition, and art style of the original image, and apply a three-dimensional focus expression with shallow depth of field.

Focus center on eyes and face. Keep pupils, eyelashes, and main facial lines clear. As you move away from the focal plane of the face, smoothly blur hair, shoulders, costume, and background according to distance. Create natural focus differences within the person as well.

Add soft foreground bokeh to hair and shoulders close to the camera, and large melting background bokeh for the background. Describe point light sources in the background as soft circular bokeh.

Illuminate hair and skin contours thinly with warm diagonal backlighting, adding subtle bloom and light bleed only to strong highlights. Maintain calm darkness in shadows to create cinematic depth that draws the eye to the face.

Uniform blurring across the entire screen is prohibited. Do not erase facial details; maintain the original line art and drawing texture.

title: Swiss Editorial Diptych with Texture Zones
description: A detailed GPT Image 2 prompt for creating a vertical diptych from an uploaded photo. The top half preserves the original image, while the bottom half applies seven experimental texture zones (Reeded Glass, Engraving, Stipple, Halftone, Pixel Mosaic, Overlay, Duotone) in a Swiss editorial style.
promptText:
Create one vertical 3:4 diptych for each uploaded photo, divided into equal top and bottom halves with a seamless join. No divider, frame, or collage. Swiss editorial design, experimental photography, and vintage print aesthetics.

TOP HALF — ORIGINAL PHOTOGRAPH
Preserve the original identity, pose, scene, composition, perspective, lighting, and colors. Allow only subtle color grading and background extension. No text.

BOTTOM HALF — SEVEN EXPERIMENTAL TEXTURE ZONES
Repeat the entire original photo. Overlay seven asymmetrical rectangular zones of different sizes directly onto the image pixels, crossing non-critical details. Maintain visual continuity inside and outside every zone. Never crop, zoom, shift, duplicate, or redraw the image. Keep all important focal features visible.

SEVEN NUMBERED TECHNIQUES

01. Reeded Glass: Vertical optical refraction.

02. Black-and-White Engraving: Fine etched lines and crosshatching.

03. American Stipple: Black-and-white microdot texture.

04. Vintage Halftone: CMYK printing dots.

05. Pixel Mosaic: Square pixel blocks.

06. Transparent Overlay: 2–4 translucent overlapping layers.

07. Duotone Screen Print: Two-color screen-printing effect.

DESIGN DETAILS
Add hairline borders, tiny corner squares, and fine leader lines to identify each rectangular zone. Label every technique with its corresponding number and English name. Keep all areas outside the seven zones photographic and realistic.

STRICT REQUIREMENTS
No logos, watermarks, extra images, or unnecessary decorative elements. Preserve the original photograph's integrity and maintain a clean, sophisticated editorial layout.

OUTPUT: One high-definition 3:4 vertical poster with equal top and bottom halves.

title: Dark Silhouette Poster Design from Photo
description: A complex prompt for transforming uploaded photos into a split-layout poster: original photo on top, flat silhouette still life on dark ground below, with specific artistic constraints.
promptText:
Please turn each uploaded photo into an independent high-end design poster, do not stitch images together, output each photo separately. Use a 3:4 vertical composition, split into two halves like a folded card, with the fold line exactly on the horizontal centerline, both halves equal height, do not draw the fold line itself.

Top half retains the original photo, preserving subject identity, structure, pose, realistic texture, natural lighting, and original color atmosphere, only applying slight high-end color grading to give it an art magazine, indie publication, and exhibition image quality. To fit the aspect ratio, naturally extend the environment background but do not stretch, distort, or change the subject; crop as panorama, leave sky above the subject's head, do not crop the top. No text in the top half, all text appears only in the bottom half.

Bottom half extracts only the most recognizable **subject, outline, structure, pose, and narrative relationships** from the photo, reconstructing them as a **Flat Silhouette Still Life on a Dark Ground**. Do not copy the photo completely, but compress the subject and a few adjacent items into flat silhouettes without outlines or internal details, making the correspondence with the top photo immediately identifiable. **Must have several unoutlined flat silhouettes overlapping into a cluster standing on a solid dark background, with only one block noticeably brightest, popping out as if lit**, this defines the style, missing it fails.

Bottom half requires new artistic judgment. Even if the original has poor composition, messy background, or small subject, save it by **removing environment, converting to front/side view, moving scattered items close into a cluster**; arrange silhouettes of varying heights staggered, as if quietly placed on an invisible surface. If the photo is a scene (street, corridor, landscape, interior), take only the most representative single object or fragment, do not draw the rest, do not draw the whole scene.

Form focuses on **unoutlined front/side silhouette blocks**: each shape expressed with one color block, soft edges with slight hand-cut undulations, almost no internal structure, only using darker same-color small blocks where necessary to indicate openings, gaps, or turns. People, animals, buildings, objects, plants, and landscapes are unified into flat front or side silhouettes, depth read only through occlusion and color shade, no perspective or projection.

Texture is **fine dry-brush gouache granules**: dark background and each silhouette covered with very fine powdery speckles, making color surfaces soft and slightly velvety; stop here, no scratches, stains, folds, or aging effects.

Composition uses **a medium-sized silhouette cluster + large dark negative space**. Bottom half drawn as **panorama**, as if photographer stepped back, subject complete with empty space around, smaller than intuition suggests; **leave sky** above subject, like mounting header wider than footer, nothing touches the central fold. Silhouette cluster slightly off-center, base line on invisible horizontal, other side left for text. Prefer things quietly crowded together rather than spread across the canvas.

Color extracted from the top photo's most emotional hues, remixed into **deep ground plus low-saturation pink-grey blocks**: darkest photo color further dimmed keeping some hue as majority background; other colors desaturated mixed with grey/white becoming soft pink-grey blocks; only one block lifted brightest near warm-white, sole highlight. Adjust warmth/coolness per photo, avoid pure black, high saturation, and gradients.

Text minimal editorial intervention, any language, no fixed title. Only one short name or word taken from specific things, places, actions, or details in the photo, no subtitles or second lines; text very small, much smaller than subject, using **thin serif uppercase glyphs** in dark space beside silhouette cluster, color one shade lighter than brightest, separated by quiet distance. No generic inspirational slogans.

Overall like a still life illustration in indie publication or art postcard: dark ground, unoutlined silhouettes, overlapping layers, one bright color plane and thin small text composing quiet, warm, slightly nocturnal atmosphere.

Avoid full scene replication, filled backgrounds, cartoonish feel, template poster look, avoid isolated silhouettes, adding outlines, multiple equally bright blocks without focus, 3D lighting, vivid candy colors, and overly neat vector edges.

title: GPT Image 2 Second World Surreal Photo Poster
description: A detailed prompt for generating surreal photo posters where the top half is a real photo and the bottom half expands into a conceptual 'second world' with mixed media elements.
promptText:
Based on each uploaded photograph, create an independent 3:4 vertical 'Second World' conceptual surrealist photo illustration poster. Output each separately, no collages. Strictly 1:1 split vertically. The top half is the original realistic photo; the bottom half is another layer of space growing from within the photo. They are not stitched together but exist as continuous presences in different narrative layers of the same moment.
The top half should faithfully preserve the original photo as much as possible, without changing the subject, action, spatial relationships, lighting, color, or texture. Only perform necessary proportional cropping and slight high-end tonal adjustments to give it a clean, restrained, publication-quality photographic feel.
The creative focus is not on the 'subject matter' but on re-understanding the visual structure. First, observe the most decisive structural clues in this photo (e.g., boundaries, slopes, water surfaces, reflections, shadows, cracks, roads, branches, clouds, contours, gaps, flow, repetitive rhythms, spatial turns, or poses). Find the part best suited to 'cross the boundary'. Then let it break through the photo's edge into the bottom half, undergoing a translation of purpose, scale, semantics, or narrative role upon entry. It's not simple extension, but transforming something real into another existence that can be used, entered, measured, salvaged, repaired, organized, borrowed, unfolded, or collected in the second layer of space.
The bottom half is a warm, quiet, off-white space with subtle paper texture and ample whitespace. It is not an illustration background or decoration area, but a place to receive the 'new logic after crossing the boundary'. The relationship follows: Reality → Crossing → Translation. The charm comes from a smart and accurate cross-layer narrative, not cute decorations.
You may add minimal black hand-drawn line art figures (0-3), few but precise. Figures are users of the second world, interacting authentically with the translated structures. Lines should be light, simple, natural, slightly handmade, not cutesy, complex, or distracting. Actions should be specific, restrained, and smart, like seriously handling a small thing inherent to this world.
You may add a short English handwritten caption, generated based on the actual 'Second World event' happening in the image. Tone should be like a casual discovery or soft narration, with a hint of humor and lingering interest. Do not write inspirational quotes, explain allegories, or use templates.
The overall style should present a synthesis of Mixed-Media Photo Illustration, Surreal Photomontage, Frame-Breaking Illusion, Trompe-l'œil, Visual Metaphor, and Conceptual Editorial Illustration. Formally cross-media collage, mechanically frame-breaking, core visual metaphor, emotional tone gentle, slight, and smart micro-surrealism.
Do not make it a template of 'photo + small people + sentence'; do not have extension without translation; do not have form without metaphor; do not force sentimentality; avoid commercial ad feel, complex illustration feel, repetitive actions, baseless decoration, mechanical collage, hard connections, or cheap healing vibes.
Final Goal:
Let viewers first see a valid real photo, then suddenly discover an element crossing into another layer of space, gaining an unexpected yet extremely natural new meaning there.
Not adding creativity to the photo, but revealing the second reality latent within it.
